lines.trans: What cocktail will you drink, Vika?
I like dry white wine.
Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!
And what will you drink yourself?
I will drink a little good juice.
Do you not drink strong drinks at all?
Tomorrow morning I need a clear head.
You take your work very seriously.
I dream of becoming the very best chef!
I like your big dream very much.
You look simply stunning tonight.
Thank you, Max, I am very pleased.
Let's go dance to this beautiful music!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: person serving drinks at the bar

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('white').

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wine glass, champagne flute, goblet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll drink from our wine glasses.
She raised a glass of champagne.

examples.text: Ничего страшного! Мы из наших бокалов выпьем.
examples.trans: No problem! We'll drink from our wine glasses.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

выпить.gloss: to drink, to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: often used without an object for drinking alcohol

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: an idiom for a big telling-off

meanings.en: 'голову оторвать' = to tear someone's head off
meanings.note: an idiom for a big telling-off

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cocktail' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какой коктейль ты будешь пить, Вика?
examples.trans: What cocktail will you drink, Vika?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: сон is a dream while sleeping

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, тебе сколько лет? Это глупые детские мечты.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, how old are you? Those are silly childish dreams.
We'll find some music right now.
I like listening to quiet music.

examples.text: Вань, посмотри! — Смотри, работает! Сейчас музыку найдём.
examples.trans: Vanya, look! — Look, it works! We'll find some music right now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Ты совсем не пьёшь крепкие напитки?
examples.trans: Do you not drink strong drinks at all?
The bartender made a delicious cold beverage.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

meanings.en: to treat, to handle, to regard (+ к + dative)
meanings.note: относиться бережно к... = to treat with care

examples.text: Он всегда хорошо относится к людям.
Книга новая, мы её только что получили. Пожалуйста, относитесь к ней бережно.
examples.trans: The book is new, we just received it. Please treat it carefully.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: The cat is under the table.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'трясающе').

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'juice' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will drink a little good juice.
Make me some fresh orange juice.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: short forms сух, суха, сухо, сухи

examples.text: Нам нужны сухие дрова для костра.
examples.trans: We need dry firewood for the campfire.
The branch is dry! Look, our scout.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dance', paired with 'станцевать'.

examples.text: Ты у нас в клубе танцевала!
examples.trans: You used to dance at our club!

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
